Hi Sam — following up with the numbers we discussed. TL;DR: H100 gives best p95 at 8k with batching tuned; single 80GB H100 is likely sufficient for your initial PoC with the right quantization and KV caching. Details below.

Benchmarks (8k sequences, mixed batch size up to 16) — measured on Redwood runtime v2.4:
- H100 (80GB), batch=8 (continuous batching): p50 ~ 110ms, p95 ~ 320ms, throughput ~ 18 tok/s per GPU for generative workloads (measured with your prompt mix).
- H100 (80GB), batch=16: p50 ~ 140ms, p95 ~ 420ms, throughput ~ 28 tok/s per GPU.
- A100 (80GB), batch=8: p50 ~ 150ms, p95 ~ 470ms, throughput ~ 12 tok/s per GPU.

Notes / recommendations:
- If p95 < 250ms is a hard SLA for the 8k long-tail, you’ll need H100 and to limit batching for interactive traffic (batch<=8) while routing async jobs to higher-batch pathways.
- KV cache yields ~15-20% p95 improvement for repeat prefixes; we recommend enabling prefix caching in the PoC.
- Quantization (int8) reduces memory footprint and increases throughput but can add ~10-30ms to p50 depending on model; we can test a quantized variant if quality is acceptable.
- For the PoC: start with single H100 80GB with dedicated pool, continuous batching up to 8, prefix caching enabled, and 95th percentile targets monitored. If you need sustained higher throughput (e.g., >50 tok/s effective), add a second GPU and use sharded routing.

Attached are raw CSVs from our run on 8k sequences and a short notes file with config snippets you can drop into your test harness.

Next step suggestion:
- 30–60 minute PoC planning call: we can provision a small dedicated pool, run your representative prompt set, and capture p50/p95 under your exact traffic mix.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
